hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext: CONDUCTOR PLUGIN DISABLED: its installed files have CRLF line endings, so its cx-* commands (cx-doctor, cx-init, cx-wsl) cannot run; they fail with errors such as env: 'bash\r': No such file or directory. Do not route work through the conductor in this session; do the work yourself. The user has been shown the fix; apply it only when the user asks: in the plugin's install folder (the installPath of conductor@conductor-for-claude-code in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json, or under CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR when that is set) run find .claude-plugin bin scripts hooks worker-shims templates skills commands -type f -exec sed -i 's/\r$//' {} +, then cx-doctor. If the plugin comes from a folder (directory) marketplace edited with Windows tools, convert that source folder the same way, or the next update copies the CRs back; for an archive install, claude plugin marketplace update conductor-for-claude-code && claude plugin update conductor@conductor-for-claude-code (or a reinstall) also works. Never use git commands inside the plugin's install folder to repair it.

systemMessage: conductor: this plugin copy has CRLF line endings, so its cx-* commands cannot run and its routing policy is off. Fix: in its install folder (the installPath of conductor@conductor-for-claude-code in ~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json) run find .claude-plugin bin scripts hooks worker-shims templates skills commands -type f -exec sed -i 's/\r$//' {} +, then run cx-doctor. A folder (directory) marketplace edited with Windows tools needs the same fix in its source folder; an archive install can instead be refreshed with claude plugin marketplace update conductor-for-claude-code && claude plugin update conductor@conductor-for-claude-code (or a reinstall).
